title: An Ice Dam Burst With 10 Times the Flow of Every River

scenes.text: An ice dam burst with ten times the flow of every river.
At the end of the Ice Age, a lake in Montana held over 500 cubic miles of water.
It was up to 2,000 feet deep, and held more water than Lake Erie and Lake Ontario combined.
A wall of ice held it back, until the wall failed.
The flood raced out at speeds approaching 65 miles per hour, and the lake could drain in just 48 hours.
It happened again and again, dozens of times. The ice always rebuilt the dam.

description:
At the end of the Ice Age, a wall of ice holding back Glacial Lake Missoula failed.
The flood ran at about ten times the combined flow of all the world's rivers, and the lake could drain in 48 hours.
Could it happen again?
first_comment: Dozens of floods like this. What natural event scares you most?
